claims.text: The eel dishes are glazed with a proprietary soy-based tare that has been replenished since founding; Japanese soy sauce tare is wheat-based, so the signature dishes are not gluten-free.
The restaurant is built around eel, conger eel, sea urchin and Seto Inland Sea seafood with fish-based dashi; there is no documented vegan preparation.

name: Tamari Ya RICE DONUT (田万里家 ライスドーナツ ekie広島駅店)

claims.text: No wheat is used in any product; the shop is a rice-flour donut specialist, so facility-wide wheat cross-contact is low. No published dedicated-fryer statement — confirm shared-oil status on the day.
Chocolate-topped varieties contain dairy (乳成分); plain varieties are dairy-free.
「生地は小麦を使用せず、全てグルテンフリーです」 — dough uses no wheat and is entirely gluten-free; eggs are not used.
ekie press release: 「生地は小麦を使用せず全てグルテンフリー」, additive-free, rice-bran oil, pesticide-free own rice.
The signature and essentially only dish is a wheat-noodle bowl, so gluten is central to the kitchen; no gluten-free handling or separate preparation is documented.
The broth is chicken-based and the standard topping is seasoned ground pork, so the dish is not suitable for vegans or vegetarians and there is no plant-based alternative noted.

name: 天麩羅 すえ廣 (Tempura Suehiro)

claims.text: All tempura is fried in wheat-flour batter in shared oil; vegetable pieces share the same fryer as seafood and chicken, so cross-contamination with gluten (and seafood) is inherent.
Tempura is accompanied by dipping sauce/soy-based seasonings that conventionally contain wheat; no wheat-free alternatives are indicated.
Vegetable tempura is fried in the same oil as shrimp, squid, fish, and chicken, and sets are served with fish-based broth and pickles, so plant items are not free of animal cross-contact.

name: 鉄板屋 我んが (Teppanya Ganga)

claims.text: Wheat-based okonomiyaki batter and wheat noodles are cooked on a shared teppan grill alongside other dishes; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Dishes use standard okonomiyaki/soy-style sauces, which typically contain wheat; no wheat-free sauce is documented.
Menu is built on meat and seafood (steak, oysters, uni) cooked on a shared grill; no vegan preparation or separation is documented.

name: 鉄板焼･お好み焼 花子 本店 (Teppanyaki Okonomiyaki Hanako Honten)

claims.text: Okonomiyaki is cooked on a shared teppan griddle alongside wheat batter, wheat noodles, and wheat-soy-sauce, so heavy gluten cross-contact is inherent to the cooking surface.
Okonomiyaki sauce and teppanyaki seasonings used in Hiroshima-style cooking are generally based on wheat-containing soy sauce.
The griddle is used continuously for pork, egg, and bonito-topped okonomiyaki, so any dish would share a surface with animal products.

name: 手打出雲そば いいづか (Teuchi Izumo Soba Iizuka)

claims.text: Soba noodles are boiled in shared water with wheat-containing items and the sauce uses wheat soy sauce; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Izumo soba tsuyu is based on standard wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free tamari is advertised.
The dipping/pouring sauce is built on fish-based dashi, so even plain soba is prepared with animal-derived broth.

name: 手作りのパン 河内ベーカリー (Tezukuri no Pan Kouchi Bakery)

claims.text: A traditional wheat-flour bakery; flour is handled throughout, so the environment is unsuitable for anyone avoiding gluten and there is no gluten-free offering.
Signature items include egg and ham-and-egg sandwiches and curry bread; egg, dairy and meat are used in the kitchen, and plain breads may share equipment, so vegans should ask about specific items.
